method: python training/confirm_ltr.py --data-dir ml-32m Today every pick is a fixed mix: 80% "viewers like you" (the routed ranking) and 20% content. Stacking many recommenders with gradient-boosted trees is a standard way to beat any single one in recommender-system challenges, so this tests it on iCinema's own models. Setup: the same 1-in-5 MovieLens 32M sample, time split, and 3,000 + 3,000 viewers as training/evaluate_blends.py; each viewer is scored from 3 random likes, like a new user. For each viewer, the 300 movies today's blend ranks highest are re-ranked. Features for each movie, all as percentiles within that viewer: the routed ranking, item-kNN, RP3beta, EASE, the content model, and popularity. The ranker (scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingClassifier, label = the viewer later rated it 4+ stars) is trained on the first 3,000 viewers only.
